**No credible new news exists regarding NSA involvement in mind control programs as of April 2026.**[1][2][3][4][7]

Recent NSA announcements focus on cybersecurity, such as Zero Trust guidelines (January 14 and 30, 2026), support for FBI warnings on Russian GRU router threats (April 7, 2026), and leadership changes like appointing Tim Kosiba as Deputy Director (January 9, 2026).[4][7] Older surveillance issues, like Section 702 renewals and historical violations, involve signals intelligence but not mind control.[2][3][5][6]

The most relevant recent development is a December 23, 2024, scholarly collection on **CIA's MKULTRA and behavioral control experiments** (e.g., LSD, hypnosis, drugs for interrogation), not NSA.[1] This documents historical CIA efforts from the 1950s–1970s, including erased records and abuses on prisoners and juveniles, but confirms no new techniques discovered.[1] No search results link the NSA to mind control, past or present; such claims often stem from unverified conspiracy theories lacking evidence in official or scholarly sources.[1][2][4]
